A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that a synthetic model of the nickel pincer cofactors in lactate racamse can function as a catalyst for lactate racemization and that the mechanism of the enzyme is most likely a hydride transfer mechanism.
the nickel pincer cofactors of lactate racemases are not only structurally similar, but also mechanistically similar to their iron analogs.
the pyridinium-based nickel pincer complexes are the first synthetic models that are both structural as well as functional mimics of the nickel pincer cofactors of lactate racemases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pyridinium ring is not required for the enzymatic function of the cofactor, and that the pyridine ring can be substituted with a variety of heteroarenes, including pyrrole.
synthetic pincer complexes can be used as models of the pincers in enzymes and as such can be used to understand the mechanisms of the enzyme reactions.
the nickel pincer cofactors of lactate racemases are not only a novel class of metallocofactors but are also functional models of the active site in the enzyme.
